title: CoBe: A Benchmark For Conversational Counterfactual Text Editing
abstract: arXiv:2610.13057v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Counterfactual text editing is the ability to revise a given text in light of a hypothetical change while preserving facts not causally affected by that change. When asked what would have happened if a doctor had not recommended surgery, the model output should retain the patient's medical history and modify only the consequences of the decision. This requires causal understanding: a model must determine, without being explicitly instructed to, what events are affected by the hypothetical change and what should remain fixed. This skill is central to human reasoning, especially in safety-critical domains like healthcare or law. By contrast, the task of associational text generation merely generates text statistically associated with the altered condition. translated_title: CoBe：面向对话式反事实文本编辑的基准测试
translated_abstract: 反事实文本编辑是指根据一个假设性变化来修改给定文本的能力，同时保留未受该变化因果影响的事实。当被问及“如果医生没有推荐手术会发生什么”时，模型输出应保留患者的病史，仅修改该决定所带来的后果。这需要因果理解能力：模型必须在没有被明确指示的情况下，自行判断哪些事件受到假设性变化的影响，哪些内容应保持不变。这项技能是人类推理的核心，尤其在医疗或法律等安全关键领域中至关重要。相比之下，关联性文本生成任务只是生成与改变后的条件在统计上相关联的文本。在上述医疗示例中，关联性响应可能会让患者的症状变得更轻，因为较轻的病例通常与不做手术相关。这样的响应会产生一个看似合理的场景……
tldr: 该论文提出了CoBe基准，用于评估模型的对话式反事实文本编辑能力，要求模型通过因果理解判断假设性变化会影响的范围，在修改文本的同时保留未受因果影响的事实，而非仅生成统计上相关联的文本。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces CoBe, a benchmark for conversational counterfactual text editing, which evaluates whether models can causally understand the consequences of a hypothetical change—revising only affected events while preserving unrelated facts—rather than merely generating statistically associated text.
